name: hero
title: Hero
description: The opening band of a marketing page: one headline, one supporting paragraph, up to two calls to action, and an optional media slot.

frame.summary: Copy and media side by side when wide, stacked copy-first when narrow. A plain section: a hero is not a widget, so it is never a Card.

regions.name: copy
regions.purpose: Eyebrow, headline, lede and the action row.
regions.collapse: Stays first in source and visually at every width.

regions.name: media
regions.purpose: A product screenshot or illustration supplied by the caller.
regions.collapse: Stacks below the copy; never above it, so the headline is the first thing a reader of either kind meets.

components.name: badge
components.for: Optional eyebrow, e.g. a release label.

components.name: heading
components.for: The headline, at the caller's level with a display role.

components.name: button-group
components.for: Holds the primary and optional secondary action.

components.name: button
components.for: The calls to action — primary first, then secondary.

components.name: link
components.for: Actions that navigate (most hero CTAs do) should be links styled as buttons.

dependsOnFuture.for: CTAs that navigate to another page are links, not buttons; today Button renders a <button>.

headingLevel.summary: The outline level of the headline (1 on a landing page); everything below it steps down from here.
use: The level the surrounding page gives this block — a template passes it explicitly.
dont: Choosing a level for its visual size. Size is the Heading component's `role`, a separate decision.
headingLevel.a11y: No default, for the reason Heading's `level` has none: only the caller knows the depth, and a skipped level breaks heading navigation for the whole page.

eyebrow.summary: A short label above the headline, rendered as a Badge.
dont: A sentence. It is a label; a sentence belongs in the lede.

title.a11y: Becomes the heading and the section's accessible name.

dont: Two paragraphs. A second one is a feature-grid or a section below.

primaryAction.summary: The one thing the page wants the reader to do.

media.summary: An image or illustration, with its own alt text.
media.a11y: Decorative media must carry alt=""; a screenshot that shows the product needs a real description.

behavior.summary: Pure composition: no state, no primitive. The only decisions are the outline, the action hierarchy and the stacking order.

decisions.decision: At most two actions, primary then secondary
decisions.why: Three CTAs in a hero is a menu. Two lets the second be a softer path without competing — Button's own contract reserves `lg` for a single prominent call to action on a marketing surface.

decisions.decision: headingLevel is required, even though it is usually 1
decisions.why: A hero is sometimes the second band of a page (a product sub-page under a site hero). Defaulting to 1 would produce two h1s silently; requiring it costs one prop.

decisions.decision: Copy is first in source at every width
decisions.why: Reading order and visual order must agree. A media-first stack on narrow screens puts an image between the reader and the headline.
Text over an arbitrary image has no verifiable contrast pairing; the token contracts can only promise text on a theme.bg.* surface.

landmarks.label: aria-labelledby the block's own heading (the headline)

obligations: Navigating CTAs must be links (`href`), not buttons with onClick.
Media needs alt text, or alt="" when purely decorative.

steps.change: One column: copy, then media. Actions wrap to full-width rows.
Two columns, copy start-aligned, media vertically centred.

responsive.notes: A container query rather than a media query, so the hero behaves the same inside a docs layout with a rail as it does full-bleed.

native.reason: Marketing composition. A native app is reached after install, so there is nothing to persuade or convert; the equivalent content in-app is an onboarding or paywall screen, which is a different block with different obligations.

tokens.band background: theme.bg.canvas (or theme.bg.subtle for an alternating band)

tokenGaps.need: A page content max-inline-size (container width) for marketing bands
tokenGaps.interim: The band's content box is capped at calc(var(--rata-size-control-lg) * 32) and centred with auto inline margins; the playground's own column cap is a literal with a comment saying there is no measure token. Open decision: a size.container.* role via the design-tokens skill, or keep deriving from the control scale.

tokenGaps.need: A section-band vertical padding step larger than space.section for marketing rhythm
tokenGaps.interim: padding-block uses var(--rata-space-section) top and bottom. space.section is the only page-rhythm step and was sized for docs pages, not full-bleed marketing bands.

tokenGaps.need: A media aspect-ratio / radius convention for marketing imagery
tokenGaps.interim: radius.container on the figure; aspect-ratio is the caller's image.

usage.when: The first band of the landing-page template.
usage.example:
<Hero
  headingLevel={1}
  eyebrow="New in 3.0"
  title="Invoices that chase themselves"
  lede="Send, remind and reconcile without a spreadsheet."
  primaryAction={{ label: "Start free", href: "/sign-up" }}
  secondaryAction={{ label: "See pricing", href: "/pricing" }}
/>
usage.notes: Spec only — the API is the thing being approved. Both actions navigate, which is why this block is blocked on Link.

openQuestions: Does a hero ever carry a form (email capture)? If so, compose newsletter-signup into the copy region rather than adding a slot.
